clue.text: Turning down a cold fruit

indicators.note: turning round the run of letters so it reads from the far end

parts.note: the French protest cry 'à bas' means down with
C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a chilly piece of fruit offered to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses everything after it: A BAS (French for 'down with'), then A, then C.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a winter melon with wrinkled yellow skin, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Groups of notes hard to get in strings

indicators.note: to get in means the letter goes inside the word for strings

parts.note: cords are strings or thin ropes
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A musician finds it hard to play some note clusters on stringed instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings' suggests violins, but it means pieces of string.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sets of musical notes sounded together, so groups of notes.

clue.text: Numerical data question over including university in band

indicators.note: including means the word for data holds a letter inside it

parts.note: stats is short for statistics, numerical data
O stands for over on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A survey question about university bands.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo are a long-running British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Status Quo is a British rock group, famous for 'Rockin' All Over the World', so a band.

clue.text: Odd note adopted by half of insects of second city

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival: belonging to the city

indicators.note: adopted by means these letters are taken inside the next piece
half of keeps only the first two letters of the four-letter word for insects

parts.note: bees are insects
rum means odd or strange
mi is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A strange musical note is picked up by insects in Britain's second city.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham is commonly called Britain's second city; its nickname is Brum.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the informal name for someone or something from Birmingham, England's second city.

clue.text: Drink for each after a vermouth I fancy at first

indicators.note: the clue gives the word for each after the a, so that piece follows it

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in the bar order 'gin and It'

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word fancy

explanation.surface: A barfly fancies a vermouth as an opening drink, ordering one per person.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is crossword shorthand for Italian vermouth, from 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate appetite.

clue.text: Growth of cultivated geranium with heads of pink and opal, planted round lake

indicators.note: planted round means the rearranged letters go round another letter
cultivated means the letters are worked and rearranged like soil
heads of takes the opening letter of pink and of opal

explanation.surface: A gardener plants pink and opal geraniums around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'geranium' looks like the definition but is anagram fodder; 'Growth' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the genus of garden plants commonly called geraniums, a kind of plant growth.

clue.text: Lowers taken aback in coarse cud eruption

indicators.note: taken aback says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is startled by a cow's crude belch.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden word: 'in' signals it, and 'taken aback' reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something is to bring it down or diminish it, a synonym.

clue.text: Literary doctor's unfinished letter

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Doctor Thorne is the title character of a Trollope novel

explanation.surface: A fictional physician never completed his letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence; it is an Old English alphabet character.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a runic character used in Old English for the 'th' sound, a letter of that alphabet.

clue.text: The setter's into islands singular beauty

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the islands

parts.note: the Farnes are islands off Northumberland
the setter is speaking of himself, 'I am', so I
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: The setter is into the islands for their unique beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Farne Islands lie off the coast of Northumberland, in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness can mean pleasing looks or a light complexion, so beauty.

clue.text: Murky old resentment apt originally for India

indicators.note: for here means one letter is put in place of another

parts.note: pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of the word apt

explanation.surface: An old grudge is tangled and murky, fitting for a story about India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apt originally for India' means the first letter of apt replaces the I (India) in PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not letting light through, cloudy and hard to see into, so murky.

clue.text: Happy island processed oil flowers

parts.note: glad means happy
I is a standard abbreviation for island on maps

indicators.note: processed means worked over, so the letters of oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful island refines its oil and grows flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tall plants of the iris family with spikes of bright blooms, i.e. flowers.

clue.text: Band leader beat senior

parts.note: to drum is to beat rhythmically
major means senior, as in an older brother at school

explanation.surface: The leader of a group outplayed someone older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band leader' looks like a pop musician; here it is the person heading a marching band.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the person who leads a marching military band, twirling a mace or baton.

clue.text: So last injury almost sorted for hacks?

indicators.note: sorted means put into order, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the last letter of injury is dropped

explanation.surface: A last injury is nearly dealt with, so is it time for some hacking?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks' could be a verb; it is the noun for writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack is an informal, slightly scornful word for a newspaper writer.

clue.text: First knight leaves gun for religious leader

indicators.note: leaves means that letter departs from the word for the gun

parts.note: a cannon is a large gun
N is the chess notation for a knight; first says it is the first of the two that goes

explanation.surface: A senior knight swaps his weapon for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral, so a church leader.

clue.text: Discontent and doubt mostly before upper-class parasite adopts new ship

indicators.note: before puts the shortened doubt ahead of the rest
mostly means all but the last letter of the word for doubt

parts.note: a query is a doubt raised
U stands for upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: adopts means the parasite takes another letter into itself

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with a parasite on a new ship has doubts and is discontented.
explanation.definitionFit: Querulousness is a complaining, peevish state of mind, a form of discontent.

clue.text: Original root gets discovered, second record concealed in two years

indicators.note: discovered means the covering outer letters of gets are removed
concealed in means the pieces go inside the pair of letters

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two of them
mo is short for moment, a second
a log is a record, as on a ship

explanation.surface: An origin is uncovered, while a second record lies hidden for two years.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymology is the study or account of a word's origins, its original root.

clue.text: Potter's art is such disappointment, no top, hardy inside and arty occasionally

indicators.note: no top means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a swiz is British slang for a swindle or disappointment

indicators.note: inside means only the inner letters of hardy are kept
occasionally means taking every other letter of arty

explanation.surface: A potter's craft is a letdown, unless they are hardy and somewhat artistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a ceramicist, but means Harry Potter. SWIZ is British slang for a cheat or letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter is a boy wizard, so his art is the practice of magic.

clue.text: Inside forwards in America bagging four — lottery is void, with no harm intended?

parts.note: in means inside

indicators.note: bagging means holding the numeral inside

parts.note: in American sport the attacking players are the offense
IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: a word that is void has lost its inside, leaving only the outer letters of lottery

explanation.surface: A sports report: American attackers bag four while a lottery is cancelled, all quite harmlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: In American sport the attacking side is called the offense, spelt with an S; 'is void' means the lottery is emptied of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting this way means doing so without offending, i.e. with no harm meant.

clue.text: Shirking from sport with man on board

parts.note: sport can mean fun or amusement
the king is a piece, a man, on a chess board

explanation.surface: Avoiding a game by playing with a fellow at the board.
explanation.definitionFit: To funk something is to avoid it out of fear, so funking is shirking.

clue.text: To embroil opponents, partners advanced both hands

parts.note: at bridge East and North are opponents, E and N
at bridge South and North are partners, S and N
R and L, right and left, are both hands

explanation.surface: A bridge player tangles with the opposition while partners raise their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the players are North, South, East and West; N and S partner each other against E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare someone in a tangle is to embroil or entangle them.

clue.text: Group succeeded without festival

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
ex means without, as in ex dividend
Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival

explanation.surface: A band did well without playing at the festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Tet is the Vietnamese lunar New Year festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six musicians or singers.

clue.text: A southern writer that's wooden

definitions.note: as an adjective the word means made of the wood of the trembling poplar

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer from the south whose prose is stiff and lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wooden' suggests a stiff writer; it defines the adjective meaning made of this poplar's wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The trembling poplar's name doubles as an adjective for things made of its timber.

clue.text: Starts to plunder effects robbers divided up in hiding

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Robbers begin to loot goods, divide them up and lie low.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means hidden or lying concealed, so lost from sight.

clue.text: Miles playing along with Geordie rock

indicators.note: playing means the letters of Miles are moved about in performance

parts.note: to can mean along with, as in 'added to'
a Geordie, someone from Newcastle, is from the North East, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A musician called Miles jams with a man from Newcastle, playing rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a person from Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England, so NE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sedimentary stone made mainly of calcium carbonate, a common rock.

clue.text: Most obscene tango to follow is tried drunk

indicators.note: to follow puts the tango letter after the rest
drunk means the letters of is tried are reeling into a new order

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drunk attempts an indecent tango.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty can mean smutty or indecent, and the superlative is the most obscene.

clue.text: Frolic about in retro vacation

indicators.note: about means the run of letters is turned round
in says the letters lie inside the phrase retro vacation

explanation.surface: Someone frolics around on a retro-style holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks letters from 'retro vacation'; 'about' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to prance and leap about in play, which is to frolic.

clue.text: Unknown tongues translated for baby

parts.note: Y, like X, is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters of tongues are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foreign languages are rendered for an infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby' is used in the family sense: the baby of the family is its last-born.
explanation.definitionFit: The baby of a family is the last-born child, the one with the fewest years.

clue.text: Pretend spread concealed in bit of butter

indicators.note: concealed in puts one word inside another

parts.note: a pat is a small piece of butter
to lay is to spread out, as in laying a cloth

explanation.surface: A spread hidden inside a knob of butter.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something only half-heartedly, as a pretence, is to go through the motions of it.
